detail: torch defaults torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_bf16_reduced_precision_reduction (and the fp16 one) to True. Flipping it moves native logits by up to 0.19; the first differing port is L0.o (the attention value mix). The flags are not in saturn_pub numeric_scope, so two runs under different flags share a fingerprint scope, and every number labelled `bound` (explain head bound, forecast _affine/_scores, reads value_mix/head_write, circuits matmul bound) assumes float32 accumulation, which is false under the default. Measured worst |eta|/bound for value_mix is 0.996: inside, with no margin.
evidence: mrun job-bcfca7e0c4ef (flag True vs False), job-c2de4323f91b (first differing port); Qwen2.5-1.5B bf16 cuda eager, beast RTX 4080, torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.13.1
next: Owner decision: record both flags in numeric_scope (changes every cut fingerprint; shared saturn_pub) and have bounds refuse or widen when a flag is True.
resolution: fixed 2026-11-13: both CUDA reduced-precision flags are in the numeric scope (saturn_pub/numerics.py); a cut refuses under a different flag and names the field; matmul bounds state their accumulation premise and are refused when it fails (analysis/accumulation.py). Real model: job-5e7d47663d29, job-2db9ca10cabc.

detail: Every trail mark holds a private clone of the full state on the device: 28,672 bytes per token row per mark at the real model's size, L+4 marks per row, retain_rows=None by default. About 80% of a mark's bytes repeat the previous mark (measured on tiny models: 79.5% qwen2 bf16, 79.8% qwen3 fp32). Generating 50 rows from 100 tokens would hold about 5.7 GB of GPU memory (formula, not measured).
next: Share unchanged per-layer tensors between consecutive cuts: the decoder cache keeps per-layer tensors, advance gets a never-writes-its-input contract (hooks and ports included), StateCut stops cloning sealed tensors, isolation tests. Or set a finite default retain_rows and rely on recipe replay for far rewinds.
resolution: fixed 2026-11-13: cuts share unchanged tensors; a mark costs what its step wrote. Tiny qwen2 bf16, 32 generated rows: held 392,128 -> 12,032 bytes, per mark 1,743 -> 54; qwen3 fp32 1,427,072 -> 41,344. In-place writes to a sealed cut are detected and refused. Receipts capped at 64; edit tensors and port caches released. Real-model memory not re-measured.

detail: whatif and reads verdicts end `unresolved` on the real model: the propagated rounding bound is not finite after a few layers (interval arithmetic through softmax and SwiGLU). Example: whatif L20.m = 0 scale -> exact 0.424, native 0.4375, `bound unresolved (the propagated bound is not finite)`; reads: `unresolved (changed, but no rounding bound to compare with)`. On tiny bf16 models the bound resolves but is vacuous (38.06 against an effect of 0.0046). So no causal verdict is ever `resolved` at scale.
evidence: mrun job-2c1cebccd74d, job-c37ca590539d; tests/repl_golden/cells_cross_run.out; Qwen2.5-1.5B bf16 cuda eager, beast RTX 4080, torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.13.1
next: Different bound: bound the difference of the edited and base chains (errors common to both cancel) or a first-order rounding model with a stated premise, instead of two worst-case chains added. Needs a math note before code.
resolution: fixed 2026-11-13: verdicts no longer depend on a worst-case rounding bound (none exists in the proofs, and one chain alone is not finite). Rule (analysis/verdict.py, P20): native change = exact float64 change + measured residual; floor = max(|residual|, 2 x dtype spacing at the consumer's logits). Real model job-dd7991c9079c: whatif replace 3.75 and mix 1.375 resolved; reads L20.h5, L21.h0, L26.h10 causal.

detail: mdb cannot yet be pointed at mrun's native runtime (QStore + paged kernels): attach() refuses anything that is not a Hugging Face module tree, and the analysis verbs read weights from HF modules. It is feasible, measured two ways. (1) Tiny Qwen2 fp32 on CPU, lossless FP32 QStore: a proxy around the store (the kernel's only weight seam: embed_rows and matmul(name, x)) leaves paged_forward_kv bitwise unchanged, stops at any of the 43 seam points and re-enters bitwise, and gives 16 ports (h a q k v qr s p A o r n g u f m) bitwise equal to mdb's engine on Hugging Face, logits included; zeroing one MLP neuron changes the logits by the same bits in both. (2) Qwen2.5-1.5B, int8 QStore, CUDA: decode token 11.9 ms, 11.8 ms through an inert proxy, 12.7 ms capturing all seam values (393 seam calls); reaching a stop from the token boundary 0.2 ms (L0) to 10.2 ms (L27); stop and re-entry bitwise; rerun bitwise; the attention replica rebuilt from the seam and the K/V arena equals the observed o_proj input exactly; K/V cell edits are a direct arena write: base margin -4.8048, effects A 3.519 / B 0.812 / A+B 4.873, interaction 0.542 (mdb on HF with re-rounded int8 weights: -4.8047, 3.517 / 0.812 / 4.871, 0.542). Kernel-vs-HF port differences on the real model (up to 1.3e-3 relative, logits 0.066) come from the weights, not the arithmetic: the store's int8 weights differ from a torch re-rounding of the checkpoint in 11k-584k elements per matrix, while store.matmul equals F.linear on the store's own weight bitwise. The int8 store is a different model from the bf16 checkpoint (margin -4.80 against -4.75; effects 3.52 / 0.81 / 4.87 against 3.75 / 1.0 / 5.125); no FP32 store of this model exists on beast. Not tested: batched kernel (batched_paged_logits), the CUDA decode graph, dense-qstore-cuda (fused SwiGLU and residual-norm kernels hide n/g/u/f), MLX, ANE, MoE kernels. mrun's `hf` backend already works unchanged (job-6470ef881011; needs attn_implementation='eager' and a dtype in model_kwargs).
evidence: tiny: results/engine-native-kernel-20261113/probe.{py,log}; real: mrun job-59747c4e848b (native_kernel.py), job-5980ca70169c (weights_equal.py); rev 6d3c765; torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.13.1, RTX 4080, mrun at /home/beast/domains/mrun
